$comment: Implements spec 03 §6 (aggregation operators: sum, mean, weighted_mean, best_n with groups, points_mean, sum_points, gpa, count_where, rubric_profile; fail_if escape hatch) and §6.1 (ranking policy). One aggregation per document; a pack lists them under aggregations.
title: Result aggregation
description: A composable operator that computes a period-level value from learning-area results and stores an explanation trace (spec 03 §6).

op.description: Operator from spec 03 §6. weighted_mean uses each learning area's coefficient; points_mean and sum_points feed a lookup scale; count_where and rubric_profile produce distributions rather than a single mark.

n.description: How many results to keep, for best_n (spec 03 §6: KCSE best 7).

value.description: Which value of each learning-area result the operator consumes, for example points for KCSE best-7 and grade_points for the Uganda PLE aggregate (spec 03 §6).

groups.description: Constraints a best_n selection must satisfy: required areas, minimum counts from a group, and where remaining places come from (spec 03 §6).

over.description: The exact learning areas the operator covers, for example the four PLE subjects (spec 03 §6). When omitted the learner's learning areas in scope are used.

fail_if.description: Escape hatch for national special cases such as a compulsory subject failure capping the division (spec 03 §6). Every such rule must cite its source and have test vectors.

weights.description: How weighted_mean obtains its weights: coefficient uses each learning area's coefficient (spec 03 §6 Francophone moyenne), or an explicit map of code to fraction.

multipliers.description: Per learning-area multipliers applied to each result before the aggregate is formed, for a rule that counts one subject more than once: DfE Attainment 8 doubles English and mathematics within the best eight. A multiplier of 2 counts the result twice and 1 is the default. Every key must be a learning area in scope (runtime check).

divisor.description: What the multiplied aggregate is divided by, so the divisor is declared rather than implied: Attainment 8 divides by ten, though only eight subjects count. sum_of_multipliers divides by the total of the multipliers, which is the weighted mean over the selected results. Required whenever multipliers is declared; without multipliers the operator's natural divisor applies (the number of selected results for mean and best_n, one for sum).

precision.description: Decimal places kept on the aggregate before lookup (spec 03 §6 examples: 2 and 3).

result_scale.description: Grading scale code used to turn the aggregate into a grade, division, mention or mean grade (spec 03 §6). The scale must be declared in the pack (runtime check).

then.description: count_where and rubric_profile produce distributions, not a single value, so there is nothing to multiply into an aggregate.

groupConstraint.description: One best_n constraint: require every listed area, take at least min from a named group, or fill remaining places from any area (spec 03 §6).

group.description: Learning-area group as declared on learning areas, for example sciences or humanities.

min.description: Minimum number of results from the group.

fill_from.description: Remaining best_n places may come from any learning area.

op.description: Post-processing applied to the operator result, for example mean of the selected points (spec 03 §6 KCSE example).

any_grade.description: Grade code that triggers the cap, for example F9.

in.description: Learning areas the trigger is limited to. When omitted it applies to all areas in the aggregation.

then_max_division.description: Highest division the learner may be awarded once the trigger fires, for example IV (spec 03 §6 PLE example).
